mechanism_narrative: A sustained increase in GDP indicates strong economic growth, which should positively impact the S&P 500 over the next 60 days.
failure_condition: If GDP growth is positive but SPX returns are negative over 60 days in more than 40% of cases.

mechanism_narrative: A decline in unemployment rate below 4.5% signals a strong labor market, leading to positive S&P 500 returns.
failure_condition: If UNRATE falls below 4.5% but SPX returns are negative in more than 50% of cases.

mechanism_narrative: When industrial production and housing starts both increase, it indicates strong economic activity, leading to positive S&P 500 returns.
failure_condition: If both indicators increase but SPX returns are negative over 60 days in more than 40% of cases.

mechanism_narrative: An increase in federal funds rate above 4% signals monetary tightening, negatively impacting S&P 500 returns.
failure_condition: If FEDFUNDS exceeds 4% but SPX returns are positive in more than 50% of cases.

mechanism_narrative: A significant increase in CPI suggests inflation, leading to potential rate hikes and negative S&P 500 returns.
failure_condition: If CPI exceeds 5% but SPX returns are positive in more than 50% of cases.

mechanism_narrative: Increasing payroll employment indicates a strong job market, leading to positive S&P 500 returns.
failure_condition: If PAYEMS increases but SPX returns are negative in more than 40% of cases.

mechanism_narrative: Increasing housing starts indicate strong demand, leading to positive S&P 500 returns over 60 days.
failure_condition: If HOUST increases but SPX returns are negative in more than 40% of cases.

mechanism_narrative: Low unemployment and high federal funds rate indicate a strong economy with potential inflation, leading to positive S&P 500 returns.
failure_condition: If conditions are met but SPX returns are negative in more than 50% of cases.
